questions.question: A scientist places a dye on top of two different solid blocks, Block A and Block B. The dye penetrates deep into Block A but remains entirely on the surface of Block B. What is the most accurate conclusion about these blocks?
options: Block A has a higher concentration of dye than Block B.
Block A is permeable to the liquid dye particles, whereas Block B is impermeable.
The particles in Block B are moving faster than the particles in Block A.
Block A is at a much lower temperature than Block B.

questions.question: An acid-indicator jelly cube is placed in a beaker of dilute acid. After 5 minutes, only the outer 2 mm of the cube has changed color. What does this observation directly show about the process of diffusion?
options: Diffusion occurs instantly throughout the entire volume of the jelly.
Acid particles move into the jelly cube gradually from the outside inwards.
The center of the jelly cube actively repels the incoming acid particles.
Diffusion of acid only happens when the jelly cube is fully dissolved.

questions.question: Two identical agar cubes containing phenolphthalein are placed in hydrochloric acid: Cube X at 10°C and Cube Y at 40°C. How will the rate of color change compare, and why?
options: Cube X will change color faster because cold temperatures make the jelly more porous.
Cube Y will change color faster because the acid particles have more kinetic energy and move quicker.
Both cubes will change color at the same rate because temperature only affects gases, not liquids in jelly.
Cube X will change color faster because the density of the acid is higher at lower temperatures.

questions.question: Three agar cubes of different sides (1 cm, 2 cm, and 3 cm) are placed in a dye. After 10 minutes, they are cut in half to measure the depth of dye penetration. Which of the following is true?
options: The dye will have penetrated to the exact same depth in all three cubes.
The dye will have reached the very center of the 3 cm cube first because of its larger volume.
The 1 cm cube will have a smaller percentage of its volume colored than the 3 cm cube.
The depth of penetration will be greatest in the 3 cm cube due to greater gravitational pull.

questions.question: In an experiment, a jelly cube placed in a warm dye becomes fully colored much faster than a jelly cube in a cold dye. Using particle theory, how can this difference be explained?
options: Warm dye particles expand and become smaller, allowing them to fit through tighter gaps.
Cold temperatures cause the jelly particles to pack more tightly, completely closing all pathways.
Warm dye particles have more kinetic energy, causing them to move and collide more rapidly into the jelly.
Cold dye particles lose their charge, meaning they can no longer attract the neutral jelly particles.

questions.question: A synthetic membrane with microscopic pores of diameter 2 nanometers (nm) is used to separate two solutions. Glucose molecules (diameter 1.5 nm) and starch molecules (diameter 10 nm) are added to one side. Which statement best predicts what will happen?
options: Both glucose and starch will pass through because they are both soluble carbohydrates.
Neither molecule can pass through because the pores only allow water molecules to cross.
Glucose molecules can diffuse through the pores, but starch molecules are too large to pass.
Starch molecules will pass through faster than glucose because they have a stronger concentration gradient.

questions.question: A selectively-permeable membrane separates a high-concentration sugar solution from a low-concentration sugar solution. The sugar molecules are small enough to pass through the membrane. Which of the following accurately describes the movement of the sugar molecules?
options: Sugar molecules only move from the low-concentration side to the high-concentration side.
Sugar molecules only move from the high-concentration side to the low-concentration side.
Sugar molecules move through the membrane in both directions, but more move from high to low concentration.
Sugar molecules stop moving entirely once the concentration on both sides of the membrane is equal.

questions.question: A bag made of selectively-permeable membrane contains a 5% salt solution. It is placed in a beaker containing a 20% salt solution. If salt particles are small enough to pass through the membrane, what is the predicted net movement of salt particles?
options: There will be a net movement of salt particles out of the bag into the beaker.
There will be a net movement of salt particles from the beaker into the bag.
There will be no movement of salt particles at all because the membrane blocks salt.
Salt particles will move in equal numbers in both directions, resulting in no net change.

questions.question: Visking tubing containing starch and glucose solutions is placed in a beaker of pure water. After 30 minutes, Benedict's test (for glucose) on the beaker water is positive, but the iodine test (for starch) is negative. What does this observation demonstrate?
options: Glucose molecules have actively transported themselves, whereas starch molecules require energy to move.
Starch molecules have decayed into glucose molecules inside the Visking tubing.
The Visking tubing is permeable to glucose but impermeable to starch.
The pure water in the beaker has pulled the glucose out while pushing starch back inside.

questions.question: Why does iodine (a small molecule) turn starch inside a Visking tubing blue-black, while the starch (a very large molecule) does not turn the iodine solution outside the tubing blue-black?
options: Iodine can diffuse through the membrane pores into the tubing, but starch is too large to diffuse out.
The membrane pores actively pump iodine inwards while blocking the outward flow of starch.
Starch is insoluble and therefore cannot move in liquid, whereas iodine is a gas.
The tubing is made of a material that chemically destroys starch if it attempts to leave.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly applies the particle model to the cytoplasm of a living cell?
options: The cytoplasm is a continuous, solid mass that does not contain individual particles.
The cytoplasm is made entirely of water particles, with no other substances dissolved in it.
The cytoplasm and all the dissolved substances within it are composed of constantly moving particles.
The cytoplasm contains particles, but they are stationary and do not move because it is inside a cell.

questions.question: Oxygen is a small molecule required by cells for respiration. How does oxygen enter a living cell?
options: It is actively pumped through large protein channels that require energy.
It diffuses through small gaps in the cell membrane from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration.
It is converted into water outside the cell so that it can dissolve the membrane.
It can only enter the cell when the cell membrane temporarily breaks open.

questions.question: Proteins are large molecules built inside cells. Why are these protein molecules unable to freely diffuse out of the cell through the cell membrane?
options: Proteins are strongly repelled by the electrical charge of the cell membrane.
Protein molecules are too large to pass through the tiny pores of the cell membrane.
The cell membrane only allows water and gases to pass through, blocking all other substances.
Proteins are instantly broken down into amino acids the moment they touch the cell membrane.

questions.question: Why is the cell membrane described as "selectively-permeable"?
options: It allows all substances to enter the cell but prevents any substances from leaving.
It only allows substances to pass through when the cell is supplied with external energy.
It allows only certain substances to diffuse through it based on properties like particle size.
It changes its structure completely to block all particles during the night.

questions.question: Inside a muscle cell, carbon dioxide is constantly produced by respiration, making its concentration high. Outside the cell, in the blood, the concentration of carbon dioxide is low. What is the net direction of diffusion for carbon dioxide?
options: Carbon dioxide will have a net movement out of the cell, down its concentration gradient.
Carbon dioxide will have a net movement into the cell, against its concentration gradient.
Carbon dioxide will not move because the cell membrane is completely impermeable to gases.
Carbon dioxide will move equally in both directions, so there is no net movement.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the behavior of individual glucose particles dissolved in water?
options: They move in straight, organized lines directly toward areas of lower concentration.
They remain completely stationary until a concentration gradient forces them to move.
They move in random directions, constantly colliding with water particles and each other.
They only move when heated, otherwise they sink to the bottom and vibrate.

questions.question: Container A holds 10 grams of salt dissolved in 100 mL of water. Container B holds 10 grams of salt dissolved in 500 mL of water. Which container has a higher concentration of salt, and why?
options: Container B, because it has a larger total volume of liquid.
Container A, because there are more salt particles in a given volume of liquid.
Both containers have the same concentration because they contain the same mass of salt.
Container B, because the salt particles are more spread out and can move faster.

questions.question: If a barrier separating a concentrated sugar solution from pure water is removed, what causes the net movement of sugar particles towards the pure water side?
options: The sugar particles are attracted by the empty space and actively pull each other forward.
The random movement of particles results in more sugar particles moving into the empty area than returning.
Gravity pulls the heavier sugar particles towards the side with more water.
Water molecules push the sugar particles forward to equalize the pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate definition of diffusion?
options: The active transport of large particles across a membrane requiring cellular energy.
The movement of water molecules from a high concentration of water to a low concentration of water through a membrane.
The passive movement of particles of a substance from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
The rapid evaporation of liquid particles from a surface due to a temperature gradient.

questions.question: Inside a cell, the concentration of oxygen is low because it is used up in respiration. Outside the cell, the concentration of oxygen is high. Predict the net movement of oxygen particles.
options: Oxygen particles will have a net movement into the cell.
Oxygen particles will have a net movement out of the cell.
Oxygen particles will move in both directions at equal rates, so no net movement occurs.
Oxygen particles will stop moving entirely because the concentration difference is too high.

questions.question: A student places a solid block of wax and a block of gelatin in water containing blue dye. After two hours, only the gelatin block is blue throughout. Which statement best explains this observation?
options: Gelatin is permeable to the dye solution, allowing its particles to diffuse through, whereas wax is impermeable.
The wax contains larger particles than the gelatin, which blocks the dye from entering.
Water molecules are too large to pass through the wax but easily dissolve the gelatin.
Gelatin actively pumps the blue dye into its structure, while wax lacks active transport.

questions.question: A student places a jelly cube containing universal indicator into an acid solution. Over time, they observe a color change moving inward from the outer edges. What does this visual boundary represent?
options: The region where the indicator has been completely destroyed by the acid.
The limit of how far the acid particles have diffused into the jelly at that point in time.
The area where the jelly has melted due to the chemical reaction with the acid.
The point where water particles are leaving the cube to dilute the acid outside.

questions.question: Identical jelly cubes are placed in equal volumes of blue dye at 10°C, 25°C, and 50°C. After 10 minutes, the cubes are sliced in half. Which prediction about the undyed core of the cubes is most accurate?
options: The undyed core will be smallest in the 50°C cube because high temperature increases particle kinetic energy and diffusion rate.
The undyed core will be smallest in the 10°C cube because colder temperatures make the jelly matrix more porous.
The undyed core will be the same size in all cubes because temperature only affects the rate of active transport, not passive diffusion.
The undyed core will be largest in the 50°C cube because heat causes the dye particles to expand and get trapped at the surface.

questions.question: Three agar cubes of different sizes (1 cm³, 8 cm³, and 27 cm³) are soaked in dye. If they are all left in the dye for the exact same duration, which cube will have the greatest percentage of its total volume penetrated by the dye?
options: The 27 cm³ cube, because its larger volume pulls more dye particles inward by gravity.
The 8 cm³ cube, because it has an intermediate surface area to volume ratio.
The 1 cm³ cube, because it has the largest surface area to volume ratio, allowing dye to reach its center faster relative to its size.
All three cubes will have the same percentage of volume penetrated because the rate of diffusion is constant.

questions.question: When acid diffuses into an alkaline jelly cube containing phenolphthalein, the pink color disappears. Which particle-level explanation best accounts for the speed of this color change increasing at higher temperatures?
options: The acid particles collide with the jelly matrix more violently, breaking it apart to create larger channels.
The acid particles gain kinetic energy, move faster, and collide more frequently, speeding up their net movement into the cube.
The heat causes the phenolphthalein indicator particles to break down, accelerating the color change.
The jelly particles expand at higher temperatures, which mechanically pushes the acid particles toward the center.

questions.question: A synthetic membrane has pores that are exactly 1.5 nanometers (nm) in diameter. Glucose molecules are 0.9 nm in diameter, while starch molecules are 5.0 nm in diameter. If a solution of both is placed inside the membrane, what will diffuse out?
options: Only glucose will diffuse out because its molecules are smaller than the membrane pores.
Only starch will diffuse out because larger molecules exert more pressure on the pores.
Both glucose and starch will diffuse out because both are soluble in water.
Neither will diffuse out because the pores must be larger than the sum of both molecular sizes.

questions.question: A Visking tubing bag filled with a 5% glucose solution is placed in a beaker containing a 5% glucose solution. Which statement correctly describes the movement of glucose molecules across the tubing membrane?
options: Glucose molecules stop moving across the membrane entirely because the concentration is equal on both sides.
Glucose molecules continue to move through the membrane, but they only move from the outside of the bag to the inside.
Glucose molecules move through the membrane in both directions at equal rates, resulting in no net change in concentration.
Glucose molecules only move outward because the pressure inside the bag forces them through the pores.

questions.question: A selectively-permeable bag containing a 20% sucrose solution is placed into a beaker containing a 5% sucrose solution. The membrane is permeable to water but impermeable to sucrose. What will be the net direction of water movement?
options: There will be a net movement of water out of the bag into the beaker to dilute the external solution.
There will be a net movement of water into the bag from the beaker, moving from a higher water concentration to a lower water concentration.
Water will move in both directions at the exact same rate, so there will be no net movement.
Sucrose will move out of the bag into the beaker until both solutions reach 12.5% concentration.

questions.question: A student sets up a Visking tubing bag containing starch suspension and places it in a beaker of iodine solution (which turns blue-black in the presence of starch). After 30 minutes, the liquid inside the bag turns blue-black, but the liquid in the beaker remains orange-brown. What does this observation prove?
options: Starch has diffused out of the bag into the beaker, but iodine was unable to enter the bag.
Iodine particles have diffused into the bag, but starch particles were too large to diffuse out of the bag.
The membrane is impermeable to both substances, and the reaction only occurred on the outer surface of the tubing.
Water has moved out of the bag by osmosis, concentrating the starch so that it changes color on its own.

questions.question: In an experiment, a Visking tubing bag filled with a concentrated salt solution is placed in a beaker of pure water. Over time, the concentration of salt in the beaker increases. Which explanation best accounts for this observation?
options: Salt ions are small enough to pass through the pores of the Visking tubing, so they move down their concentration gradient into the beaker.
Water molecules have reacted with the Visking tubing, creating larger holes that allow the salt to leak out.
The Visking tubing has actively pumped the salt ions into the beaker using energy from the surrounding water.
The salt ions have dissolved the Visking tubing membrane, allowing the entire solution to mix freely.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the physical nature of a cell's cytoplasm in relation to diffusion?
options: Cytoplasm is a continuous fluid containing no individual particles, which allows nutrients to glide through without friction.
Cytoplasm is made up of moving particles, including water and dissolved solutes, which constantly collide with diffusing substances.
Cytoplasm is a solid structure where particles are fixed in place, preventing any internal movement of molecules.
Cytoplasm is a vacuum that pulls external substances inward through the cell membrane by suction.

questions.question: Oxygen is vital for cellular respiration. How does oxygen enter a muscle cell from the surrounding blood capillaries?
options: It is actively pumped through specialized protein valves that require energy.
It dissolves the cell membrane lipid layer permanently to create temporary pathways.
It diffuses down its concentration gradient through tiny microscopic pathways in the cell membrane.
It is carried into the cell inside vesicles by endocytosis.

questions.question: Why are large protein molecules synthesized inside a cell unable to leave the cell by simple diffusion through the cell membrane?
options: Protein molecules are too large to pass through the tiny pores of the cell membrane.
Proteins are insoluble in water and cannot move unless they are in gaseous form.
The cell membrane only allows positively charged ions to pass through its pores.
Inside the cell, proteins are held in place by strong magnetic forces that prevent passive movement.

questions.question: A cell membrane is described as "selectively-permeable." What does this term mean in the context of cellular transport?
options: The membrane allows all substances to pass through at the same rate regardless of particle size.
The membrane acts as a solid wall that completely blocks all substances from entering or leaving.
The membrane allows only certain substances to diffuse through its pores, while blocking others based on properties like size.
The membrane only allows water to pass through, completely blocking all other small molecules and ions.

questions.question: A cell has a high concentration of carbon dioxide inside its cytoplasm compared to the surrounding tissue fluid. What will be the net movement of carbon dioxide?
options: Carbon dioxide will show a net movement out of the cell, down its concentration gradient.
Carbon dioxide will show a net movement into the cell, up its concentration gradient.
Carbon dioxide will not move because the cell membrane blocks all waste products.
Carbon dioxide will move into and out of the cell at equal rates with zero net movement.

questions.question: Why do individual perfume particles eventually spread throughout a still room even though there is no wind?
options: The particles are attracted to the walls of the room by gravitational forces.
The particles move in random directions, constantly colliding with air particles and bouncing off in new directions.
The particles naturally repel each other, forcing them to move in straight lines directly away from the source.
The particles are lighter than air, so they rise to the ceiling and then fall down uniformly.

questions.question: Container A has 10 dye particles in 100 mL of water, while Container B has 50 dye particles in 100 mL of water. Which statement correctly compares their concentration?
options: Container A has a higher concentration because the dye particles have more space to move around.
Container B has a higher concentration because there are more dye particles per unit volume of water.
Both containers have the same concentration because the volume of water is identical.
Container B has a lower concentration because the dye particles are packed too closely to dissolve.

questions.question: A drop of food coloring is carefully placed at the bottom of a glass of still water. Over time, the color spreads evenly. Which statement best describes the "net movement" during this process?
options: Dye particles move only upward because gravity does not affect dissolved particles.
There is an overall movement of dye particles from the region of high concentration at the bottom to the region of low concentration at the top.
Dye particles move randomly, but water particles push them all to the top of the glass.
Dye particles only move towards areas where there are other dye particles of the same type.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most accurate definition of diffusion?
options: The active transport of molecules across a cell membrane requiring energy from ATP.
The passive movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
The movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a membrane.
The rapid streaming of cytoplasm inside a living cell to distribute nutrients.

questions.question: A single-celled organism is placed in an environment where the concentration of oxygen is extremely low compared to the inside of the cell. What will happen to the net movement of oxygen?
options: Oxygen will continue to enter the cell because cells always absorb oxygen regardless of external concentration.
Oxygen will show a net movement out of the cell into the environment, down its concentration gradient.
The cell membrane will close all its pores to prevent oxygen from escaping, resulting in zero movement.
Oxygen will be actively pumped into the cell to maintain metabolic activities without any loss.

questions.question: A student places a drop of blue ink onto two different solid blocks: Block A is made of waterproof plastic, and Block B is made of agar gel. The ink stays on the surface of Block A but spreads through Block B. What property must Block B have to allow this?
options: It must be actively transporting the ink particles.
It must be impermeable to the liquid ink.
It must be permeable to the liquid ink.
It must be colder than Block A.

questions.question: In a practical investigation, a jelly cube containing an indicator is placed in an acid. After some time, the outer edges of the jelly cube change colour, while the very centre remains unchanged. What does this observation show about the process of diffusion?
options: Diffusion occurs instantly throughout the entire volume of the jelly cube.
The acid particles enter the jelly from the outside and gradually move inwards.
The jelly particles are moving out of the cube into the acid faster than the acid moves in.
The indicator prevents the acid from reaching the centre of the cube.

questions.question: Two identical jelly cubes are placed into beakers of blue dye. Beaker A is kept at 5 degrees Celsius, and Beaker B is kept at 40 degrees Celsius. After 15 minutes, both cubes are cut in half. What would you expect to observe?
options: The dye has penetrated further into the cube from Beaker B than the cube from Beaker A.
The dye has penetrated further into the cube from Beaker A than the cube from Beaker B.
The dye has penetrated to the exact same depth in both cubes.
No dye has entered either cube because temperature does not affect liquid diffusion.

questions.question: Three different-sized agar jelly cubes (1 cubic centimetre, 8 cubic centimetres, and 27 cubic centimetres) containing an alkaline indicator are placed in a container of acid. After 5 minutes, which cube will have the highest percentage of its volume reached by the diffusing acid?
options: The 27 cubic centimetre cube because it has a larger surface area to absorb the acid.
The 8 cubic centimetre cube because its intermediate size balances volume and surface area.
The 1 cubic centimetre cube because the acid has a shorter distance to travel to reach its center.
All three cubes will have the exact same percentage of their volume reached.

questions.question: When the temperature of a liquid surrounding a jelly cube is increased, the liquid diffuses into the jelly faster. How can particle theory explain this observation?
options: Higher temperatures make the jelly particles expand and block the pathways of the liquid.
Higher temperatures give the liquid particles more kinetic energy, so they move and collide faster, increasing the rate of diffusion.
Higher temperatures cause the liquid particles to stick together, making them pass through the jelly more easily.
Higher temperatures reduce the gravity acting on the liquid particles, allowing them to float into the jelly.

questions.question: A membrane contains microscopic pores of a specific size. If starch molecules are large polymers and glucose molecules are small simple sugars, which of the following will occur when a mixture of both is placed inside the membrane?
options: Both starch and glucose will diffuse out through the pores easily.
Only glucose molecules will diffuse out because they are small enough to fit through the pores.
Only starch molecules will diffuse out because their larger size forces them through.
Neither molecule will diffuse out because membranes only allow water to pass.

questions.question: A selectively-permeable membrane separates two solutions of oxygen. There is a higher concentration of oxygen on Side A than on Side B. Which statement correctly describes the movement of individual oxygen particles?
options: Oxygen particles move only from Side A to Side B.
Oxygen particles move only from Side B to Side A.
Oxygen particles move in both directions across the membrane, but more move from A to B than B to A.
Oxygen particles do not move at all once a concentration difference is established.

questions.question: A bag made of a selectively-permeable membrane contains a 5% glucose solution. It is placed in a beaker containing a 20% glucose solution. If glucose can pass through the membrane, what will be the direction of the net movement of glucose particles?
options: Net movement of glucose will be out of the bag into the beaker.
Net movement of glucose will be from the beaker into the bag.
There will be no net movement because the concentrations are already in dynamic equilibrium.
Glucose will move in equal numbers in both directions, so there is no overall trend.

questions.question: A piece of Visking tubing is filled with starch solution and placed into a beaker of iodine solution. Iodine particles are small enough to pass through the tubing, but starch particles are too large. What would you expect to observe after 30 minutes?
options: The solution inside the Visking tubing turns blue-black, while the beaker remains orange-brown.
The solution in the beaker turns blue-black, while the inside of the tubing remains cloudy white.
Both the inside of the tubing and the beaker turn blue-black.
No colour change occurs anywhere because Visking tubing is completely impermeable to all substances.

questions.question: In an experiment, Visking tubing filled with a concentrated glucose solution is placed in a beaker of pure water. After 20 minutes, glucose is detected in the beaker water. How can this observation be explained?
options: The Visking tubing broke down and dissolved in the pure water.
Glucose molecules moved by active transport from the lower concentration to the higher concentration.
Glucose molecules diffused down their concentration gradient through the tiny pores in the Visking tubing.
Water molecules pushed the glucose molecules out of the tubing through force of gravity.

questions.question: When we study diffusion in biological cells, we must remember that the cytoplasm inside the cell is not a continuous, uniform solid, but is actually:
options: A single giant molecule that cannot be divided.
An empty space where nutrients are stored as energy waves.
Made up of many individual particles, including water and dissolved substances, that are constantly interacting.
A solid block of jelly that has no free-moving particles.

questions.question: Oxygen is vital for respiration in animal cells. How does oxygen enter a cell from the surrounding blood capillaries?
options: It is pumped through large protein channels using energy from respiration.
It diffuses through small holes in the cell membrane down a concentration gradient.
It is swallowed by the cell membrane wrapping around it in a bubble.
It cannot enter the cell directly and must be converted into carbon dioxide first.

questions.question: Inside a muscle cell, there are large protein molecules and small mineral ions. Why are the large protein molecules unable to diffuse out of the cell into the tissue fluid, even if their concentration inside is very high?
options: Protein molecules are too large to fit through the small holes in the cell membrane.
Protein molecules are repelled by the electrical charge of the cell membrane.
The cell membrane actively traps proteins using energy.
Proteins can only move through the membrane when the cell is dividing.

questions.question: Why is the cell membrane described as selectively-permeable?
options: It allows all substances to pass through freely to keep the cell in balance.
It allows only certain substances to pass through while preventing others, based on factors like particle size.
It is completely impermeable, blockading the cell from its external environment.
It only permits substances to leave the cell, but never allows them to enter.

questions.question: A cell has a carbon dioxide concentration of 2% inside its cytoplasm, while the surrounding fluid has a carbon dioxide concentration of 0.04%. What will be the net movement of carbon dioxide?
options: There will be a net movement of carbon dioxide out of the cell, down the concentration gradient.
There will be a net movement of carbon dioxide into the cell, down the concentration gradient.
There will be no net movement because the membrane blocks all carbon dioxide.
Carbon dioxide will actively be pumped into the cell against the concentration gradient.

questions.question: If you could track a single perfume particle diffusing through the air in a room, what would its path look like?
options: A straight, direct line from the bottle to the opposite wall.
A series of random, zig-zag movements caused by constant collisions with air particles.
A circular orbit around the source of the perfume.
A downward curve towards the floor due to gravity, with no horizontal movement.

questions.question: Beaker A contains 10 grams of salt dissolved in 100 ml of water. Beaker B contains 10 grams of salt dissolved in 500 ml of water. How do the concentrations of salt particles in the two beakers compare?
options: Beaker B has a higher concentration because it has more total volume.
Both beakers have the same concentration because they contain the same mass of salt.
Beaker A has a higher concentration because there are more salt particles per unit volume of water.
Neither beaker has a concentration because salt does not form particles when dissolved.

questions.question: What does the phrase down a concentration gradient mean in the context of particle movement?
options: Particles move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
Particles move from an area of lower concentration to an area of higher concentration.
Particles move downward towards the ground due to gravitational forces.
Particles move faster when they are in a highly concentrated solution.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key feature of diffusion?
options: It is an active process that requires energy from cellular respiration.
It is a passive process that relies on the random movement of particles from higher to lower concentration.
It only occurs in solid materials when they are heated.
It requires a living cell membrane to take place and cannot occur in non-living systems.

questions.question: A scientist treats a cell with a chemical that makes its cell membrane completely permeable to all substances. What is the most likely consequence for the cell?
options: The cell will function better because it can import nutrients much faster.
The cell will lose its ability to control what enters and leaves, leading to cell damage or death.
The cell membrane will become twice as thick to protect the cell.
The cytoplasm will turn into a gas and evaporate.
